secondaryWeapon: Deimos Sage Shield, later converted to Astra Arcane Shield
archetype: Teleport-based Explorer mage with a strong 2-minute burst, a good full-rotation DPM profile for solo bossing, and the longest bind in the game. Damage is gated on a freeze-stack resource: ice skills apply stacks, lightning skills consume them, and several passives pay out only while stacks are up. Easy mobbing, simple burst, cheap to bring online, which also makes it a commonly recommended boss mule and champion mule.

linkSkill.name: Empirical Knowledge
linkSkill.effect: Passive. Attacks have a 31% chance at master level to identify the weakness of the struck enemy with the highest Max HP, granting +5% damage and +5% enemy DEF ignored per stack for 10 seconds. Stacks up to 3 times, one stack per unique Explorer Magician job character on the world.

priority.node: Build the four boost node groups that feed the 6th job mastery cores first: (1) Chain Lightning, (2) Frozen Orb + Blizzard, (3) Lightning Orb, (4) Thunder Sphere + Elquines.
priority.why: These are the four of six boost node groups that matter. Each one is tied to one of the class's four HEXA mastery cores, so boost node investment is also the gate on 6th job progress. The class doc states the class has four boost nodes that must be upgraded first; Grandis Library tiers these same four above the remaining two; NamuWiki independently describes exactly four 'essential' reinforcement cores out of six and pairs each with the mastery core it unlocks.
priority.consensus: strong - three independent sources agree on which four groups matter and on the group contents (class doc, Grandis Library, NamuWiki KMS)

priority.node: Leave the remaining two boost node groups (Frost Ward + Ice Strike, and Thunder Bolt + Cold Beam) for last.
priority.why: Grandis Library ranks both in its lowest tier. NamuWiki notes one narrow exception: Ice Strike is used in some training builds before HEXA Frozen Orb is unlocked, after which it stops mattering.
priority.consensus: moderate - two independent sources (Grandis, NamuWiki); the Ice Strike training exception is single-source and KMS-side

priority.node: Level nodes for shard efficiency rather than pushing each skill to 25 before starting the next.
priority.why: The class doc advises spending shards on a slightly lower-priority skill when that skill will gain levels faster, rather than forcing strict priority order.

priority.node: Park Mana Overload at level 1, 10 or 20 before eventually pushing to 30.
priority.why: Mana Overload grants +1% final damage at every tenth level only. Levels between those breakpoints contribute nothing, so shards are better spent elsewhere until you can clear the next breakpoint.
priority.consensus: weak - single source (class doc), but stated as a flat mechanical fact rather than an opinion

priority.node: Craft Decent Holy Symbol as early as possible; later max Erda Fountain, Decent Holy Symbol, and Rope Lift / Blink.
priority.why: Decent Holy Symbol is called out as an early training priority for EXP and drop rate. Maxing Erda Fountain improves the odds of one- or two-shotting mobs. Rope Lift and Blink give free stat and magic attack when maxed.

priority.node: V skill (5th job) leveling order, KMS-side claim only: Bolt Barrage > Jupiter Thunder > Spirit of Snow = Frost Ark.
priority.why: NamuWiki states the reinforcement priority for the 6th job enhancement cores matches the 5th job order, and gives that order explicitly. The GMS Heroic class doc has its own V-skill priority chart but publishes it only as an image, which could not be transcribed, so this ordering is NOT confirmed for GMS Heroic.
priority.consensus: weak - single source, KMS balance, machine-translated; flagged contested

trios.trio: Chain Lightning / Thunder Sphere / Lightning Orb
trios.label: Trio #1
trios.why: Listed as one of two recommended boost node trios for Arch Mage (I/L). No bossing/mobbing split is given for this class on that reference.
trios.consensus: weak - single source, independently authored but dated 2024-11-21

trios.label: Trio #2
trios.why: The second of the two recommended trios from the same reference.
trios.consensus: weak - single source, independently authored but dated 2024-11-21

vMatrix.notes: Two different things are described here and should not be confused. Grandis Library and NamuWiki describe boost node GROUPS, i.e. which skills a single node type boosts: Chain Lightning alone; Frozen Orb with Blizzard; Lightning Orb alone; Thunder Sphere with Elquines; Frost Ward with Ice Strike; Thunder Bolt with Cold Beam. mystyjl instead describes TRIO packing, i.e. which three skills to keep together on one trio node. The two views agree on which six skills matter. The trio packing is the weaker claim: it is dated 2024-11-21 with underlying test data from 2024-05-14, and the class doc's own changelog records a V-matrix change on 2026-06-19 ('changed to be in line with the changes to V-Matrix'), so the packing predates a known regrouping and should be re-verified before use. Grandis Library's Primary/Secondary/Other tier labels did not extract consistently across two reads of the same page for nodes 2 and 4; the group CONTENTS were identical both times, so the groupings are recorded as reliable and the tier labels are not recorded at all.

order.step: Unlock the four mastery cores before unlocking Sol Janus.
order.why: The class doc recommends unlocking Sol Janus after the masteries are unlocked. The four mastery cores are HEXA Chain Lightning, HEXA Frozen Orb / HEXA Blizzard, HEXA Lightning Orb / Cryoshock, and HEXA Thunder Sphere / HEXA Elquines.
order.consensus: moderate - the ordering advice is single-source (class doc); the identity and contents of the four mastery cores are confirmed by three independent sources

order.step: Optional swap: unlock HEXA Frozen Orb before HEXA Chain Lightning if training matters more to you than bossing.
order.why: The class doc states this makes training much easier. HEXA Frozen Orb enlarges Frozen Orb and stops it halting at platform edges or slowing on normal monsters, which is what turns it into a strong mobbing skill.
order.consensus: weak - single source (class doc), but stated as an explicit player-choice branch rather than a fixed order

order.step: Max HEXA Stat I after Jupiter Thunder Boost is unlocked. Max HEXA Stat II after Thunder Sphere reaches level 9.
order.why: These are the two explicit HEXA Stat entry points the class doc gives in prose, describing where the Stat upgrades sit inside its own priority chart.
order.consensus: weak - single source (class doc), but text-confirmed rather than inferred from an image

order.step: Take Sol Janus after the masteries. If you train more than roughly 30 minutes a day, push it to level 10 or 20 early; level 30 only if you grind heavily.
order.why: Sol Janus grants bonus EXP with meaningful jumps at those level thresholds, and gives a choice of two mobbing modes (Dusk, an area meteor effect on a three second cooldown; Dawn, additional summons scaling from one at level 1 to three at level 20+).

order.step: CONTESTED - HEXA enhancement (boost) core order, KMS-side claim: Bolt Barrage Boost > Jupiter Thunder Boost > Spirit of Snow Boost = Frost Ark Boost.
order.why: NamuWiki reasons that these four cores carry no option other than final damage, so their reinforcement order simply follows the 5th job skill order. This is a KMS-balance claim. The GMS Heroic class doc's own chart could not be read, and its prose places Jupiter Thunder Boost early enough to gate HEXA Stat I, which does not obviously match putting Bolt Barrage Boost first. Do not treat this as settled for GMS Heroic.
order.consensus: weak - single source, KMS balance, machine-translated, and in unresolved tension with the GMS doc's prose

hexa.notes: IMPORTANT GAP, recorded rather than filled. The authoritative GMS Heroic HEXA investment order for this class exists and is credited inside the class doc to a community member named Ebola, but it is published only as an infographic image. The image was retrieved and inspected: it is a sequence of roughly 130 skill icons each annotated with a target level, captioned 'Made for Reboot by Ebola'. The icons are not individually identifiable at the published resolution, so the step-by-step order is NOT reproduced here. Guessing it would have been fabrication. What the class doc says about the chart in prose IS recorded: it is ordered by final damage per Sol Erda Fragment across a full rotation; it deliberately parks each skill at major breakpoints rather than chasing many small ones; and it optimises full rotation rather than burst, so a player who cares more about burst should weight Origin (Frozen Lightning) levels and Jupiter Thunder levels more heavily than the chart does. Node structure is fully name-validated: the origin skill is Frozen Lightning and the ascent skill is Parabolic Bolt; the four enhancement cores are Frost Ark Boost, Bolt Barrage Boost, Spirit of Snow Boost and Jupiter Thunder Boost; the common cores are Sol Janus (Dusk/Dawn) and Sol Hecate (Styx/Charon/Phlegethon). NamuWiki additionally lists a third skill core that is not yet live in GMS, matching the class doc's own 'Future Changes' entry for the KMS MapleStory Overdrive update.

priority.stat: Critical Rate to level 7 (9% crit rate)
priority.why: The class doc's stated route to exactly 100% critical rate is the baseline account sources it lists, plus 3% from Familiar Badges, plus 9% from level 7 Critical Rate hyper stat. Hyper stat and Legion are interchangeable contributors here, so points can be moved out of critical rate if Legion covers it.

hyperStats.notes: No full hyper stat allocation order is recorded, because none could be sourced. The class doc publishes its hyper stat and critical rate figures as images and its prose gives only the critical rate target. The doc explicitly says the hyper stat versus Legion split for critical rate should be optimised per character with Maple Scouter rather than read off a fixed list. That deferral is itself the finding: a static hyper stat priority list for this class is not what the maintainers recommend. A useful class-specific detail that IS text-confirmed: because Infinity was changed into a passive skill, Legion critical rate blocks became affordable for I/L, which changes how much hyper stat needs to go into critical rate compared to older guides. If critical rate is short on a less progressed account, the doc suggests the Phantom link skill as a temporary substitute until other sources come online.

passives.why: Gives I/L one of the longest teleports in the game. Note it behaves as a toggle dragged from the skill tab onto the keyboard layout, not as a passive, and it does not stack with Teleport Boost - only one of the two can be active.
passives.consensus: moderate - class doc and Grandis Library list the same five picks, but Grandis credits its build to the class doc so this is one source family

passives.why: Named by the class doc as one of the three best damage increases and described as always taken.
passives.consensus: moderate - class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent)

passives.why: The class doc calls this the +1 Hit line and groups it with Chain Lightning Reinforce and Frozen Orb Reinforce as the three best damage options, always taken.
passives.consensus: moderate - class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent)

passives.why: Third of the three damage lines the class doc says should always be taken.
passives.consensus: moderate - class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent)

passives.why: Taken as the fifth slot by default rather than because it is needed - the class doc says I/L has sufficient mobbing without it. The only real alternative is Frozen Orb - Spread, which helps mobbing slightly once HEXA Frozen Orb is unlocked.
passives.consensus: moderate - class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent); the doc itself presents this slot as flexible

hyperSkills.notes: Five passive picks total. The fifth slot is the only genuine decision: Chain Lightning - Spread by default, Frozen Orb - Spread if you value mobbing and have HEXA Frozen Orb unlocked. No sourced recommendation on the active hyper skills was found, so that field is left empty.

lines: Damage to abnormal status afflicted monsters
bossing.why: The class doc names these three as the ideal bossing inner ability and describes the rolling order around them. Grandis Library lists the same three lines, with the third at +8%, but credits its inner ability section to the class doc, so it is a restatement rather than a second opinion.
bossing.consensus: moderate - one source family (class doc, restated by Grandis Library); the three lines are text-confirmed in the doc's prose, not read off an image

earlyGame.why: The class doc explicitly warns against chasing the ideal bossing inner ability as a new player because of the cost, and names either of these single lines as a good early-game result while money goes into gear instead.

training.why: Since multiple inner ability presets became available, a dedicated grinding preset is standard. The class doc's grinding preset is published as an image and could not be read; these specific lines come from Grandis Library, which credits the class doc.
training.consensus: weak - one source family, and the underlying doc's own version of this preset was not readable

rollingStrategy.why: Roll first for Boss Damage +10%, which is the harder line to hit, using Miracle Circulators on a second preset so the working inner ability is preserved. Miracle Circulators are the route of choice in GMS Heroic because they are purchasable with meso in the Cash Shop, they are the only way to reset inner ability without spending honor (which is scarce on Heroic), and they always roll the top value for a line - Unique Boss Damage otherwise ranges from 5% to 10%. Budget around 5 billion meso on average, with 10 to 20 billion realistic on bad luck. Then wait for a discounted honor event, lock the boss damage line, and roll the remaining two lines. A separate party-bossing preset is worth keeping if you regularly party with attack speed buffers such as Buccaneer.

innerAbility.notes: The doc's ideal-bossing and grinding presets are both published as images; the three bossing lines above are recovered from the doc's surrounding prose, which names each of them, not from the image. The party-bossing preset's exact contents could not be read and are not recorded.

gearingNotes: STAFF, NOT WAND - this is the class-specific gearing call most likely to be got wrong. A wand offers extra critical rate, but the class doc says the staff's higher base magic attack outweighs it. The common counter-argument that a staff's slower weapon attack speed is a drawback is wrong for a mage: mages use casting speed, not weapon attack speed, and casting speed has a base attack speed level of 4 regardless of which weapon is held. ATTACK SPEED - the GMS cap is 10 and I/L reaches it from the sources the doc lists; the soft cap of 8 cannot be broken without a Green Potion, so a Green Potion is part of the endgame buff set rather than optional. CRITICAL RATE - the target is 100%. The doc's route is the baseline account sources it lists plus 3% from Familiar Badges plus 9% from level 7 Critical Rate hyper stat. Because Infinity was reworked into a passive skill, Legion critical rate blocks became affordable for this class, so critical rate can be shifted between hyper stat and Legion; the doc recommends optimising that split with Maple Scouter rather than fixing it. Phantom link skill is a stopgap for less progressed accounts. SECONDARY - Deimos Sage Shield, crafted from a recipe dropped by Cygnus. It is preferred over magic book secondaries because it can be starforced to 20 stars, giving more magic attack and stat. It later converts to the Astra Arcane Shield; a shield above 15 stars can only transfer into a Stage 2 or higher Astra Arcane Shield, and a fully starforced transfer costs around 10 billion meso. On Interactive servers the shield is cheap on the Auction House. WSE - the target is 9 lines of attack across weapon, secondary and emblem, but the doc says to check Maple Scouter for whether boss damage lines beat attack lines on your specific setup, and not to worry about temporarily settling for a boss line on the Genesis weapon or the shield. COOLDOWN HAT - a -2s line is the standard because it smooths the burst rotation. I/L does not directly profit from cooldown reduction the way some classes do, so casual players clearing around the 15 minute mark can stay on a stat hat. Late and endgame players may want -4s on Heroic or -5s on Interactive for tight-timer fights such as Baldrix, Limbo and Seren. Note the doc's own update on this: once the KMS change reducing the maximum boss timer to 20 minutes lands, the threshold for squeezing in an extra burst becomes -6s, so the doc's recommendation is to stay at -2s rather than buy an intermediate cooldown hat, unless you specifically want a dedicated culvert hat. FREEZE STACKS - the resource the whole kit is built on. Ice skills apply stacks, lightning skills consume them, and Frozen Orb used off cooldown is the primary source. The payouts are: +20 final damage from Storm Magic at one or more stacks; +10% critical damage from Frost Clutch at five stacks, rising to 16% with Glacial Fury at 2% per stack; +1% final damage on lightning skills per stack consumed; and +10% ignore DEF from Shatter, rising to 16% with Glacial Fury at 2% per stack. Glacial Fury also raises the stack cap from 5 to 8, which is what scales all of the above. Notably Jupiter Thunder is net positive on stacks - it consumes 6 over its full duration but returns about 21 on average, because a stack is only consumed every third proc while Blizzard can final-attack on every proc.

commonMistakes.mistake: Picking a wand over a staff for the extra critical rate.
commonMistakes.why: The staff's higher base magic attack is worth more than the wand's critical rate.

commonMistakes.mistake: Avoiding a staff because its weapon attack speed is slow.
commonMistakes.why: Mages use casting speed, not the weapon's base attack speed, so the weapon's attack speed rating is irrelevant. The doc calls this out specifically as a common misconception.

commonMistakes.mistake: Sending every V skill node straight to level 25 in strict priority order.
commonMistakes.why: Shards go further if spent on a slightly lower-priority skill that will gain levels faster.

commonMistakes.mistake: Levelling Mana Overload through its non-breakpoint levels.
commonMistakes.why: It only pays out at every tenth level, so levels 2 through 9, 11 through 19 and 21 through 29 do nothing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Chasing the perfect bossing inner ability as a new player.
commonMistakes.why: The doc is explicit that it is very expensive and that meso and honor are better saved for gear upgrades and a discount event; a single good line is the correct early target.
With the 20 minute boss timer change, the threshold for gaining an extra burst moves to -6s, so cooldown between -2s and -6s buys nothing. Stay at -2s.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forcing the mini-burst when it would desync the 2 minute cycle.
commonMistakes.why: The doc says I/L's mini-burst is not very impactful and recommends skipping it rather than delaying, both to keep the 2 minute burst on schedule and to avoid dragging out a party run.

commonMistakes.mistake: Letting freeze stacks lapse and overthinking how to maintain them.
commonMistakes.why: The doc's position is that there is no technique to it - Frozen Orb used off cooldown is the primary source and is sufficient.

sources.what: The Arch Mage (Ice, Lightning) class doc, maintained by PommeCuite (Discord zatchounet) for the Explorer Mage Discord, inherited from Vivillon. Scoped explicitly to GMS Heroic and Interactive. The authoritative judgement source for this class: boost nodes, V-skill priority, HEXA matrix priority (chart credited to Ebola and captioned 'Made for Reboot'), HEXA stat, hyper skill passives, attack speed, critical rate, inner ability, legion grid, link skills, freeze stack mechanics, burst order and rotations, culvert, and a boss/champion mule assessment. MAJOR LIMITATION: every ordered priority list in this doc is published as an embedded image, not text. Retrieve as plain text with /export?format=txt; the /mobilebasic and normal document URLs return less. The HEXA priority image was extracted and inspected but its ~130 icon steps are not individually identifiable, so the ordering is not transcribed anywhere in this file.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
defects: innerAbility.training records 'Drop Rate +20%' as the second line, sourced solely to Grandis Library. Grandis actually says 'Meso Obtained/Item Drop Rate +20%, Meso Obtained/Item Drop Rate +15%, Damage to Normal Monsters +8%'. The second line is +15%, not +20%, reflecting the real second/third-slot value cap. As recorded, the file describes an inner ability that cannot be rolled. This is the only place a number was altered rather than dropped.

'so boost node investment is also the gate on 6th job progress' (vMatrix.priority[0].why) states a gating mechanic no source asserts. The class doc, asked in two separate reads, presents boost nodes and mastery cores as separate upgrade tracks and never says one gates the other. The group-to-core alignment is real and wiki-confirmed; the causal gate is invented connective tissue.
clearedOnInspection: NO fabricated node or skill names were found. Every name in the file was checked against maplestorywiki raw wikitext and confirmed: Frost Ark, Bolt Barrage, Spirit of Snow, Jupiter Thunder, Frozen Lightning, Parabolic Bolt, all four HEXA Enhancement Boost cores, all six boost node groups with contents, Empirical Knowledge (Master Level 9 / 31% / +5% / 3 stacks, verbatim correct), and all freeze-stack values (Frost Clutch 2%/stack, Shatter 2%/stack, Storm Magic 20 FD, Glacial Fury cap 5-to-8). The fourth mastery core HEXA Thunder Sphere / HEXA Elquines, which I initially suspected was fabricated, is confirmed real by the wiki.
